newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX vols wane as dollar keeps to ranges.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX vols wane as dollar keeps to ranges.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/pair options softened Friday as the spot dollar held to narrow ranges but remained under pressure versus the mark.
One-month dollar/mark volatility slipped to 8.10/8.40 percent from 8.40/8.65 percent the previous session, and one-year dollar/mark was about unchanged at 9.00/9.30 percent.
Mark firmness on European crosses and in active mark/yen trading this morning capped the dollar, options traders said.
Dollar/mark continued to erode, with 1.7050 an important level to watch on the downside, options traders said.

Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer's comments late Thursday that the central bank was not interested in the mark weakening further, and escalating political dissent over EMU, supported the mark, traders said.

While options analysts said they looked for more weakness in dollar/mark, direction for dollar/yen near term was less clear. Dollar/yen volatility values also declined, but appeared to be catching up with dollar/mark, they said.
One-month dollar/yen volatility was at 8.30/8.60 percent late morning, down from 9.00/9.25 percent the previous session. One-year dropped 3.5 point to 9.80/10.00 percent.

Dollar/yen continued to hover just under 126.00 yen at midday. The question for dollar/yen is whether central bank intervention will quash the dollar should the market attempt another push above 127.00, one bank analyst said.

An options desk manager at a U.S. bank said he expected dollar/yen to retest the upside next week, reaching 128.00 to 129.00. Traders will be watching the impact on spot dollar of a short-dated "reverse knockout" option, valued between $500 million and $1 billion, that was purchased within the past week, he said. The option has a trigger near 127.50 yen, at which point it ceases to exist.

The buyer of the option can be expected to try to defend the position by selling dollars if the spot nears the trigger, while the seller will attempt to push it through the strike. If that happens, he said, dollar/yen could quickly advance to 128.00.
Analysts said the approaching Group of Seven meeting next weekend likely would keep volatilities underpinned.
Dollar/yen risk reversals narrowed back to around par after a shift to yen calls earlier in the week. Calls were still a slightly more expensive purchase, at 0.1/0.2, traders said.
Dollar/mark risk reversals were flat to bid for mark puts, they said.
